newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Arafat tells Netanyahu to state settlement plans.
newsitem.headline: Arafat tells Netanyahu to state settlement plans.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat has demanded Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu clearly state his settlement policy in the wake of a minister's plans for a new Jewish community on occupied Arab land.
"Arafat sent a letter to Netanyahu asking him to clearly state his settlement policy and to stop statements like those of Sharon," Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said on Thursday.
Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon said recently that planning was underway for a new Jewish settlement in the occupied West Bank, captured by Israel in 1967.
Erekat told Reuters he passed the letter for Netanyahu to his Israeli counterpart during talks on Wednesday.

The Israeli Housing Ministry has confirmed it is planning a new settlement near the West Bank Palestinian town of Ramallah but said it had many approval stages to pass and the government had yet to give its blessing.

Netanyahu, who rejects the concept of returning occupied Arab land, on Thursday met Jewish settler leaders who complain he is not pushing settlement enough. He pledged to personally address their concerns.

"The participants in the meeting agreed to continue meeting with the prime minister in a regular way to solve bureaucratic problems...The prime minister said he would continue to deal with the issue personally," said a statement from Netanyahu's office.

After meeting Netanyahu, Jewish settler Aharon Domb told Israel Radio: "We very much hope we will not have to demonstrate against the Netanyahu government...For the meantime, we've suspended protest activities...that were organised for today until next week."
Netanyahu, after coming to power in June, lifted a freeze on settlement imposed by the previous government, but has so far approved only expansion of existing settlements.
A new settlement on occupied land would require government approval but expansion of existing settlements can be approved by Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai.

"It (the government) has not decided either for or against new settlements but it has established the right of Jews to live in Judea and Samaria," Netanyahu's communications director David Bar-Illan told Reuters, using biblical names for the West Bank.

Bar-Illan said the decision by Sharon and the housing ministry to plan a new settlement did not mean it was a government decision: "It is an announcement of intent. It is not even a government proposal yet."

Some 130,000 Jews have settled among nearly two million Palestinians in the Gaza Strip and the West Bank, excluding Arab East Jerusalem, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war. A larger number of Jews have settled in East Jerusalem.
Palestinians view settlement as a provocation and vehemently oppose its expansion on lands where they hope to build an independent state.
